# iliad-026 — review, pass 1 (Iliad 4.457–544)

Edited `units.json` in place by script; `t` and every other key untouched (checked unit by unit against a copy of the draft; `t` re-checked against the packet's lines, `ln` against where each unit starts, `l` line count against `t`). Severity: major = wrong Greek/English or a false claim that misleads; moderate = a false label, a table or published-English departure, or a case relation lost; minor = wording, consistency, precision.

Counts: major 0 · moderate 10 · minor 19.

## Checked and found sound

- Every grammatical label in every note was checked against the form in its line (case, number, tense, mood, voice, elision, augment, dual, tmesis, movable ν). Apart from the items above all are true. In particular: ἕλεν unaugmented; ἕλκε, λίπε, βῆ, στῆ, ἅμαρθ’ unaugmented; λελιημένος perf. mid.; κεκάδοντο reduplicated aor. mid.; ἐξεφαάνθη singular with neuter plural; ἔβαλεν/οὖτα aorists looking back; πάγη aor. pass.; πελεμίχθη, χασσάμενος; εἰληλούθει plpf.; τετάσθην dual plpf.; βεβλήκει plpf.; ὄφρα + opt. (purpose, 466) and + subj. (486); the optatives of 539–542.
- Word-placement claims (αἰχμή only in 461; Πείροος at 525; Διώρης = the Epean leader of 537; "the line above/next line" claims; the speech beginning at 509 and ending at 513) and cross-references (461 = 503 = 526; 464 = 2.541 iliad-012; 462/493 ἤριπε; 470/524 θυμός; 469/525 οὐτάω; 497/535 χάζομαι; 536/544 τείνω; 504 = Od. 24.525, odyssey-119 ln 524, English identical; 2.844 below) hold.
- The 2.844 cross-reference in the 4.520 note: iliad-015 ln 844 is αὐτὰρ Θρήϊκας ἦγ’ Ἀκάμας καὶ Πείροος ἥρως, so "the Thracians and Peirous are in the Trojan Catalogue at 2.844" is true. Aenus as a Thracian town is correct.
- Greek → `l` word by word, then `l` ↔ `i`: no further errors of case relation, tense, mood or particle. Every row of new-renderings.md was compared with the unit; all stock epithets are translated each time (ἱπποδασείης, κρείων, μεγάθυμος ×3, φαίδιμος, ἠΰκομος, διογενής, αἴθων, αἴθοψ, κυδίστη Τριτογένεια, δεινὸς θεός, ἱππόδαμοι, χαλκοχιτώνων ×1, ὄβριμον, ἴφθιμος, ἀγαυός). The Odyssey's "Zeus-sprung"/"Zeus-born", "fire-faced"/"has the look of fire", "most glorious Tritogeneia", "shameless"/"ruthless" stones, "fell from his hand" (νεκρὸς δέ οἱ ἔκπεσε χειρός, cf. odyssey-066) all agree.
- Repeated lines: 464 = published iliad-012 (`l` "Chalcodon’s son, commander of the great-hearted Abantes," used as is); 504 = odyssey-119 (`l` and `i` identical word for word); 461/503/526 give the same English at all three places; no whole unit repeats a published Iliad unit.
- Quotation marks: “ on the `mark` unit 509 (in `l` and `i`); ” on 512 (end of Apollo's speech, `l` and `i`). The unit at 507–508 ending "shouting:" correctly has none; no speech runs in from iliad-025 (its last unit, 4.456, carries none) and none runs on into 545 (the part ends with narrative).
- `p` flags: 457, 473, 514, 517, 527, 539 match the packet's ¶ marks; `ln` of every unit matches the line it starts in.
- Scansion: the packet flags no line; none scanned.

## Findings considered and refused

- Drafter's doubt, 4.457 `i`: "kill a Trojan" is right (Τρώων with ἄνδρα); only the `l` was misleading, and is fixed.
- ἀκρόκομοι → "topknotted": the note already says the exact fashion is not known and gives the literal ἄκρος + κόμη; the rendering is the drafter's one guess, listed in new-renderings.md. Kept.
- ἐδνοπάλιζεν → "tossed about": uncertainty stated in the note; one guess, listed. Kept.
- ἀζομένη → "drying out": a rare word; "dry up" is the usual explanation and the note now says so. Kept; the glossary keeps ἄζομαι apart from ἅζομαι "dread".
- πρῶτον at 4.480: the Greek can mean "first (of his blows)", "first, before the others", or "in the front rank"; the note says the line does not decide, and `l` and `i` now both keep "first" in the neutral place. Kept.
- πέσσει → "cooks" in `l`, "broods over" in `i`: the Greek metaphor is cooking and is kept in `l`; "broods" is the table's decision (the note says what the figure means). Kept.
- θαλερός → "flourishing" (persons), βέλος → "shaft(s)": both follow the tables (θαλερὸς γάμος "blooming" is reserved; βέλος "shaft" is iliad-001's/iliad-022's, not the Odyssey's "arrow/missile"). Kept.
- πεφύκει at 4.483: published iliad-022 (ln 109) and odyssey-022/-024 all call it a pluperfect, "had grown"; the draft agrees in `l` and the note now says why `i` has "has grown". Kept.
- Ἐπειῶν "Epeans" and "bronze-shirted" at 536: the Epeans are the men of Elis (stated), epithet translated. Kept.
- 4.517 `l` "his portion bound": "his" is supplied to give Διώρεα's fate a possessor; the table row is "portion bound". Kept.
- 4.533 `l` "there stood around him companions": "him" supplied for περίστησαν; the note says "they stood around". Kept.
- 4.487 ἣ μέν τ’ … "and it": the μέν answers τὴν μέν of 485; no change needed.
- 4.532 `i` "But he did not strip off": δέ as "but" after the kill; kept.
- Table's αἴγειρος "poplar": the glossary's "black poplar" is a dictionary gloss, not a rendering; kept.

# iliad-026 — review, pass 2 (glossary and new-renderings)

Checked all 211 novel entries in `gloss.json` and the 12 `__broaden__` entries it came with against the line(s) each form stands in: lemma, case/tense/mood/number, Attic equivalent, homographs, and format (lemma — meaning; parse; typographic ’ only; under 230 characters, longest 149; no line numbers, backticks or "here"). Mechanical checks: the 211 keys equal `novel-forms.json`; every broadened entry contains the old entry whole. The known forms (234) were also read against the lines, because a known entry that does not fit this part must be broadened (5 more found below). `gloss.json` was edited in place by script (copy compared afterwards: 3 novel entries and 2 old broadened entries changed, 5 broadened entries added; key order unchanged); `units.json` and every `t` untouched.

Counts: major 0 · moderate 4 · minor 6 (10 changes in `gloss.json`); 4 rows in `new-renderings.md`.

## gloss.json changes

| entry | severity | what was wrong | what was done |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀπεσσύμενον (4.527) | moderate | "pres. part."; it is the perfect middle participle (ἔσσυμαι), present in sense (the published Odyssey entries for ἐσσυμένως say the same). | `perf. part. mid. masc. acc. sg. (ἔσσυμαι), epic -σσ-, present in sense: ’rushing away’`; the unit note now agrees. |
| ἀκρόκομοι (4.533) | minor | "with hair gathered on the crown" states as fact what the unit note says is not known. | `with hair on the top of the head, perhaps in a top-knot (ἄκρος + κόμη; the fashion is not known)`. |
| ὀνόσαιτο (4.539) | minor | Meaning order and translation ("would scorn") against the unit's "make light of" and the Odyssey table. | `make light of, scorn, find fault with … ’would make light of’`. |
| __broaden__ τέ | moderate | The new reading "(ἀτάρ τέ οἱ ’and to it’)" mistranslates: τε is the epic particle of what is always so, and the branches are the tree's: ἀτάρ τέ οἱ ὄζοι "but its branches". | `(ἀτάρ τέ οἱ ὄζοι ’but its branches’, τε being the epic particle of what is always so, not translated)`. |
| __broaden__ ὑπὲρ | minor | Example "στέρνον ὑπὲρ μαζοῖο ’the chest above the breast’" reverses the pair (στέρνον breast, μαζός nipple). | `’the breast above the nipple’`. |
| __broaden__ ἀγήνωρ (new) | moderate | Known entry is the adjective ἀγήνωρ "lordly"; 4.467 has the Trojan Ἀγήνωρ, a proper name. | Old entry whole + ` · also the proper name Ἀγήνωρ — Agenor, a Trojan leader; masc. nom. sg.` |

## Findings considered and refused

- All other novel entries checked against their line and left alone: lemma, parse and Attic equivalent right. Particular checks: βλῆτο (root aor. mid., passive sense; matches the corrected unit note), τέταντο / τετάσθην (plpf.), εἰληλούθει, ἐξέταμ’ (ἐκτέμνω as the Attic-form lemma), περίστησαν (root aorist, intransitive), ἔπλεθ’ / γένεθ’ (elided and aspirated before a rough breathing), ἅμαρθ’, ἀκοντίσσαντος, πετάσσας, ἐρύσσατο, κάππεσεν, οὖτα, ἔβαλέν, ὠκειάων (with the mare remark), τένοντε / ἀμφοτέρω (acc. dual), σφείων, ἑτάροιο (gen. of cause), ὑσμίνῃ, ὄχθῃσιν, λᾶας, αἴγειρος "black poplar" (dictionary gloss), νεμέσησε "be indignant" (a glossary meaning, not a rendering), ἠΐθεον, ἧκεν (ἧκα, as in the Odyssey entry).
- Proper-name spellings in the glossary (Simoeisios, Democoon, Peiros, Pergamos) differ from the units' Latinised forms; the existing Iliad glossary already has Peiroos beside the unit's "Peirous", so the glosser follows precedent. Left.
- Broadened entries (θαλερὸν, θυμόν, πριαμίδης, πᾶσαι, περὶ, τῷ, ἄντιφος, ἅλιον, ἐσθλὸν, ἠϋκόμοιο): each new reading fits the line it comes from and keeps the old entry whole.
- Known forms not listed above were checked against their lines (prepositions in tmesis, the pronoun/relative forms ὃ, ὅ, οἳ, οἵ, ἣ, ἥ, τά, τώ, κεν, ὡς, τις, μὰν/μέν, παρά/ὑπό/ἀμφί/ἐπί/κατά/διά) and the existing entries cover their use here; no further broadening needed. ἣ (4.487, 4.502) "it" is covered by the demonstrative "she".
